requirements.requirement: inventory-api runs on node1 as a managed (systemd) service with a healthy baseline
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-api.service created with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started; systemctl status shows active/enabled, oom_score_adj confirmed -1000 on the running PID, and /health and /inventory respond correctly before any disruption.

requirements.requirement: When a memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory, the kernel's OOM killer selects that hog process (not inventory-api)
requirements.summary: An unprotected transient unit (memhog, default oom_score_adj=0) was launched and allowed to consume memory to exhaustion under real global OOM conditions (swap disabled). dmesg directly shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1811 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0', matching memhog's PID exactly, confirming the kernel chose the hog and not the protected service.

requirements.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout the OOM event
requirements.summary: Polling during the memory-exhaustion event shows inventory-api remaining active the whole time, with /health returning the original PID (1717) and continuously growing uptime as memory climbed to 1.7Gi/1.9Gi and the hog was killed; health check afterward also succeeds.

requirements.requirement: System restored to a normal state after the OOM demonstration (swap re-enabled, transient hog cleaned up, service still healthy)
requirements.summary: swapon -a restored the original 2G swap (0 used), the transient memhog unit/script were cleaned up, and inventory-api remained active with correct persisted /inventory data.

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery (service, data, cluster state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (368725cb...) and healthy enabled/active service were captured; 'sudo -n reboot' returned an acknowledgement before the connection dropped (confirmed by subsequent connection-reset/timeout errors); post-restart boot_id (cfb8c08c...) differs from pre-restart and matches the fixed after-executor snapshot; inventory-api auto-started with OOMScoreAdjust still -1000, /health and /inventory (with original persisted data) responded correctly, and swap was correctly restored (2G, 0 used).

overall_summary: The executor deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed, OOM-protected service on node1 and directly demonstrated, via dmesg and live polling, that a real global out-of-memory event kills the unprotected memory-hog process while inventory-api keeps serving without interruption. Swap disable/re-enable used to trigger the OOM was bounded and fully restored. The independent node-restart protocol is also fully evidenced: differing boot IDs, service auto-start, persisted data, and restored swap after reboot. No unnecessary or unremediated mutations were observed.
limitations: The OOM demonstration ran with swap disabled, which is a reasonable and disclosed method to force a fast, deterministic global OOM event, but it means the specific behavior under a slower, swap-present OOM approach was not separately observed.
Only a single reboot cycle was captured; long-term durability of the OOM protection across multiple future memory-pressure events cannot be verified from this evidence alone.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to a clear purpose: service deployment (cmd-b960bd5530124e3a), a bounded swapoff/swapon pair used only to make the global OOM demonstration fast and deterministic and fully reverted (cmd-c7904a38a86a4b0d restored by cmd-25264540d7214e65), transient memhog unit creation and cleanup (cmd-c7904a38a86a4b0d, cmd-25264540d7214e65 removes /opt/memhog.py and resets the transient unit), and the mandatory reboot (cmd-07103347a56b4524). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows no failed services, only the expected new listening socket on 8080, and only transient systemd-private tmp dirs / reboot.log as residue, all expected from the deployed service and the reboot itself.
